    6. Sets `flg[j][i]` to True for each pair of indices (bug is here).
    7. Reads an integer Q from input.
    8. For each of the Q queries, reads two integers A and B.
    9. Checks if `flg[A-1][B-1]` is True.
    10. If True, prints the value of A.
    11. If False, prints the value of B.

The `flg` matrix is unnecessary and incorrectly used. The intended behavior is to directly compare the indices A and B to determine which is smaller, as this directly indicates which person is closer to the front. The current logic mistakenly uses a matrix to store boolean values, which complicates the process and introduces errors. The repair involves removing the `flg` matrix and directly comparing the indices A and B to determine the correct output.
